Simulating ORION-10

Source: vignettes/orion10.Rmd
orion10.Rmd

simulate_ldl(n, study = "orion10") makes up LDL cholesterol data that looks like the ORION-10 trial. This article explains how. It lists each number the simulation uses, where the number came from, and what was assumed.

The data is simulated. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the trial’s sponsor.

The trial

ORION-10 (NCT03399370) tested inclisiran, a drug that lowers LDL cholesterol, against placebo. It randomized 1,561 adults with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: 781 to inclisiran and 780 to placebo. Doses were given on Days 1, 90, 270 and 450.

The trial’s statistical analysis plan (SAP) defines the main analysis as a mixed model for repeated measures (MMRM). The outcome is the percent change in LDL from baseline at each visit. The model has fixed effects for treatment, visit, treatment by visit, and baseline LDL. It uses an unstructured covariance, REML and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom.

Sources

  1. The SAP: https://cdn.clinicaltrials.gov/large-docs/70/NCT03399370/SAP_001.pdf
  2. The FDA statistical review, which covers ORION-9, -10 and -11: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2022/214012Orig1s000StatR.pdf
  3. The NEJM paper’s Supplementary Appendix: https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1912387

Each number below is labelled with its source. “Read by eye” means it was read off a published figure, to about 1 point for means and 0.05 for standard deviations (SDs). “Assumed” means no public source gives it.

The data 

library(clinique)

set.seed(1)
ldl <- simulate_ldl(1561)
head(ldl)
#>   subject_id  treatment age  sex  race   visit day ldl_baseline
#> 1   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 150 150     84.68047
#> 2   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 270 270     84.68047
#> 3   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 330 330     84.68047
#> 4   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 450 450     84.68047
#> 5   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 510 510     84.68047
#> 6   001-0001 Inclisiran  78 Male White Day 540 540     84.68047
#>        ldl ldl_pct_change
#> 1 25.36234      -70.04937
#> 2 39.64797      -53.17932
#> 3 23.01864      -72.81706
#> 4 30.83611      -63.58534
#> 5 15.58256      -81.59841
#> 6 18.90423      -77.67581

There is one row per subject per visit. The visits are Days 150, 270, 330, 450, 510 and 540. LDL was also measured on Day 90, but the SAP leaves Day 90 out of the model (SAP Section 6.4.6.1), so the data leaves it out too.

There are no missing values. Real trials lose subjects, but this data is meant for practising the analysis, not the handling of missing data.

How each part is simulated

Treatment

Subjects are randomized 1:1. When n is odd, the extra subject gets inclisiran, as in the trial (781 vs 780).

Demographics

Age, sex and race come from Table 5 of the FDA review. The two arms are pooled, because differences between randomized arms are chance.

  1. Age: a normal distribution with mean 66.1 and SD 8.9, cut to the range 35 to 90 and rounded. Table 5 gives the mean, SD and range; the normal shape is assumed.
  2. Sex: 69.4% male (1,083 of 1,561).
  3. Race: 85.7% White, 12.6% Black, 1.7% Other (1,338, 197 and 26 of 1,561).

Baseline LDL

Baseline LDL comes from a log-normal distribution with mean 104.6 mg/dL and SD 38.3 (FDA review, Table 5). A log-normal fits LDL: it is never below zero and has a long right tail, like the real values (median 94, maximum 466).

Percent change at each visit

The mean percent change for each arm and visit comes from Figure 2 of the FDA review, read by eye:

day inclisiran placebo
150 -59.4 1.2
270 -48.3 4.8
330 -56.0 5.8
450 -46.0 3.0
510 -56.3 1.4
540 -53.8 1.8

Inclisiran’s values follow the dosing schedule. The drop is deepest 60 days after a dose (Days 150, 330 and 510) and weaker just before the next dose (Days 270 and 450).

These targets are the means of the values the trial observed. They are not the published estimates in Table 10 of the FDA review. Those estimates fill in missing values in a cautious way that pulls inclisiran toward zero. For example, Table 10 gives -51.4% for inclisiran at Day 510, while Figure 2 shows about -56.3%. The simulated data has no missing values, so it matches what was observed. As a result, the simulated treatment effect is a few points larger than the published one.

Spread and correlation

The simulation works on the log of the ratio LDL / baseline, not on the percent change itself. For example, a log ratio of -0.69 is a ratio of 0.5, which is a -50% change. This has two benefits:

  1. LDL is always above zero. A normal draw of percent change could fall below -100%, which would mean negative LDL.
  2. The changes are right-skewed, like the real ones. Figure S3, Panel B of the NEJM appendix shows each subject’s observed Day 510 change. Both arms have a long right tail.

The SD of the log ratio for each arm comes from the quartiles in that figure, read by eye:

  1. Placebo: quartiles about +11%, -5% and -16%, so an SD of about 0.21.
  2. Inclisiran: quartiles about -43%, -59% and -72%, so an SD of about 0.53.

The figure only covers Day 510, so the same SD is used at every visit (assumed).

Values from the same subject are correlated: someone whose LDL is high at Day 150 tends to be high at Day 270 too. No source gives the correlations, so they are assumed: 0.7 for visits 180 days apart, higher for nearer visits and lower for farther ones.

Day 150 Day 270 Day 330 Day 450 Day 510 Day 540
Day 150 1.00 0.79 0.70 0.55 0.49 0.46
Day 270 0.79 1.00 0.89 0.70 0.62 0.59
Day 330 0.70 0.89 1.00 0.79 0.70 0.66
Day 450 0.55 0.70 0.79 1.00 0.89 0.84
Day 510 0.49 0.62 0.70 0.89 1.00 0.94
Day 540 0.46 0.59 0.66 0.84 0.94 1.00

Each subject’s six log ratios are drawn together from a multivariate normal distribution with these SDs and correlations.

Taking the exponential of a log ratio pulls the average percent change up. To correct for this, each log-scale mean is lowered by half the variance (sd^2 / 2). With that correction, the expected percent change equals the target.

LDL at each visit

LDL at a visit is the baseline LDL times the ratio. The percent change is 100 * (ldl / ldl_baseline - 1).

Checking the means

The simulated means land close to the targets:

observed <- aggregate(ldl_pct_change ~ visit + treatment, data = ldl, FUN = mean)
reshape(observed, idvar = "visit", timevar = "treatment", direction = "wide")
#>     visit ldl_pct_change.Placebo ldl_pct_change.Inclisiran
#> 1 Day 150               1.505769                 -58.25524
#> 2 Day 270               5.386907                 -46.56692
#> 3 Day 330               6.601761                 -55.17030
#> 4 Day 450               3.209258                 -45.38831
#> 5 Day 510               1.821706                 -55.51716
#> 6 Day 540               1.832897                 -53.00408

Fitting the SAP’s model

The SAP’s MMRM, fitted with the mmrm package:

ldl$subject_id <- factor(ldl$subject_id)

fit <- mmrm::mmrm(
  ldl_pct_change ~ treatment * visit + ldl_baseline + us(visit | subject_id),
  data = ldl,
  reml = TRUE,
  method = "Kenward-Roger"
)

The treatment difference at each visit:

means <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ treatment | visit)
diffs <- summary(emmeans::contrast(means, "revpairwise"))
diffs
#> visit = Day 150:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -59.8 1.16 1559 -51.635 <0.0001
#> 
#> visit = Day 270:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -51.9 1.36 1560 -38.165 <0.0001
#> 
#> visit = Day 330:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -61.8 1.22 1559 -50.824 <0.0001
#> 
#> visit = Day 450:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -48.6 1.34 1560 -36.176 <0.0001
#> 
#> visit = Day 510:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -57.3 1.20 1560 -47.578 <0.0001
#> 
#> visit = Day 540:
#>  contrast             estimate   SE   df t.ratio p.value
#>  Inclisiran - Placebo    -54.8 1.25 1560 -43.733 <0.0001

The trial had two co-primary endpoints:

  1. The percent change at Day 510. The SAP’s main analysis for this is an analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) on Day 510 alone; the MMRM is one of its sensitivity analyses.
  2. The time-adjusted percent change: the average over the visits after Day
    1. The MMRM is the SAP’s main analysis for this.
c(
  day_510 = diffs$estimate[diffs$visit == "Day 510"],
  time_adjusted = mean(diffs$estimate)
)
#>       day_510 time_adjusted 
#>     -57.33066     -55.70184

The Figure 2 targets give about -57.7 at Day 510 and -56.3 time-adjusted. The published estimates, which fill in missing values, are -52.3 and -53.9 (FDA review, Table 10).

What is assumed

  1. The correlation between visits.
  2. The same SD at every visit.
  3. The normal shape of the age distribution.
  4. Every number read by eye from a figure carries some reading error.
